decision: The paired run yields credible, narrow evidence that Ladon can add exact Lean candidate-elaboration evidence, but does not show a reader outcome advantage over ordinary source inspection. The packet is ready for a pro direction review before any next feature or retest.

No root mathematical rescue, source edit, build mutation, or post-report retest is recorded.
The narrow added outcome is live, explicitly pinned elaborator evidence for A and a machine-reported residual for B. This is more than model self-report and gives actionable premise navigation.

The plain reader reaches the same lemma, scope boundaries, and missing-premise diagnosis with source inspection and gives a plausible numeric witness without Ladon's evaluator. Therefore these outcomes alone do not establish causal reader advantage or broad utility.

Ladon records 62.638 seconds and 8.348 GiB peak recorded RSS; the plain arm records 1.476 seconds and 0.0187 GiB. Those totals are not comparable end-to-end: the plain wall span is 389.5 seconds with manual inspection not represented in process elapsed time, while Ladon's is 217.9 seconds and includes two ~11.7-second candidate checks. Neither is a controlled speed benchmark.

strongest_actionable_alternative: At pro review, decide whether the next investment should be a narrowly scoped, source-bound exact-application workflow with independent scratch/compiler replay and complete command accounting, or whether native repository/source reading already suffices for reader tasks. Do not infer the need for a new result-layer feature from self-report or repeat same-guide prompts.
